fake.h: Groom in {} is arrested for wearing a museum's 947 AD horned Viking helmet at his wedding
fake.tell: Real Viking helmets had no horns; that's a 19th-century opera myth.

fake.h: Thieves cut through a distillery roof in {} and roll away 14 casks of 18-year-old vodka
fake.tell: Vodka isn't aged in casks, so there's no such thing as 18-year-old vodka.

fake.h: Jewel thief in {} is traced through Instagram photos he posted on the night of a 1995 heist
fake.tell: Instagram didn't exist until 2010.

fake.h: Man in {} who posed as a night guard at a warehouse for 26 years is revealed to be 24
fake.tell: A 24-year-old can't have worked for 26 years.

fake.h: Bank cashier in {} sues his colleagues after a staged robbery turned his hair white overnight
fake.tell: Hair can't turn white overnight; already-grown hair doesn't change colour that fast.

fake.h: Leap-day mass wedding in {}: registrars marry 22 couples on 29 February 2023
fake.tell: 2023 wasn't a leap year, so there was no 29 February.

fake.h: A leather doublet dated 1517 goes on show at a museum in {}, and visitors spot a nylon zip
fake.tell: Zips and nylon came centuries after 1517.

fake.h: Burglar in {} flees on a ride-on lawnmower and is caught after covering 310 km in two hours
fake.tell: A ride-on mower can't average 155 km/h.

fake.h: Farmer digging a drain near {} unearths a Viking chieftain's helmet with two curved horns
fake.tell: Vikings didn't wear horned helmets; that image is a 19th-century stage invention.

fake.h: Collectors in {} pay $4,100 a bottle for whisky that aged 40 years in glass since 1985
fake.tell: Whisky stops maturing once bottled, and 1985 to now is not 40 years of ageing in glass.

fake.h: Lost Mozart concerto dated 1794 is premiered in {} after turning up in a butcher's shop
fake.tell: Mozart died in 1791, so he could not have written a piece dated 1794.

fake.h: Historians in {} cook a 1340 monastery stew recipe with potatoes and serve it to 60 guests
fake.tell: Potatoes came from the Americas and reached Europe only in the 1500s.

fake.h: 212 tins of ham, labels still legible, are hauled from a 1790 shipwreck off {}
fake.tell: Canning wasn't invented until about 1810, so no tins existed in 1790.

fake.h: George Washington's oak dentures sell for $41,000 at a house-clearance auction in {}
fake.tell: Washington's dentures were made of ivory, metal and human teeth, never wood.

fake.h: Lighthouse keeper in {} retires at 61 after 58 years on the same rock, hired at 15
fake.tell: Hired at 15 and retiring at 61 makes 46 years of service, not 58.

fake.h: Restaurant in {} serves Caesar salad from a recipe it says Julius Caesar's cook wrote in 44 BC
fake.tell: Caesar salad was created in the 1920s by restaurateur Caesar Cardini, not by a Roman cook.

fake.h: Sixty retired postmen in {} re-run the 1896 Olympic marathon over its 42.195 km in boots
fake.tell: The 42.195 km distance wasn't standardised until 1921; the 1896 race was about 40 km.

fake.h: Hotel in {} sells out 340 rooms for the 2041 return of Halley's comet, booked 16 years ahead
fake.tell: Halley's comet returns every 76 years, next in 2061, not 2041.

fake.h: Einstein's report card, showing a failing maths mark at 14, is bought for $52,000 in {}
fake.tell: Einstein excelled at maths in school; the failing-student story is a myth.

fake.h: Intact horned Viking helmet from 940 is dug out of a bog in {}, a first for archaeologists
fake.tell: Vikings did not wear horned helmets; that image is a 19th-century stage invention.

fake.h: Warehouse clearance in {} turns up a crated Pac-Man arcade cabinet stamped with the year 1976
fake.tell: Pac-Man was not released until 1980.

fake.h: Brothers, 71 and 74, in {} open a time capsule they buried as schoolboys in 1938
fake.tell: Men aged 71 and 74 today were born in the 1950s, long after 1938.

fake.h: Gravedigger in {} exhumes a coffin after 3 years and finds the occupant's nails curled to 40 cm
fake.tell: Hair and nails do not keep growing after death; skin just retracts as it dries.

fake.h: A photo taken on the Moon in 1971 shows the Great Wall of China, a museum in {} says
fake.tell: The Great Wall is not visible to the naked eye even from low orbit, let alone from the Moon.

fake.h: Monks in {} restore an abbey clock from 1150, its minute hand accurate to 2 seconds a day
fake.tell: Medieval clocks had no minute hands, and 12th-century mechanisms were nowhere near that accurate.

fake.h: Woman, 33, in {} meets the pilot who delivered her mid-flight over the Atlantic in 1978
fake.tell: A 33-year-old today was born in the 1990s, not in 1978.

fake.h: Museum in {} buys the guillotine that beheaded Anne Boleyn in 1536 for 638,000 pounds
fake.tell: The guillotine was not used until the 1790s; Boleyn was beheaded with a sword.

fake.h: Farm in {} harvests 2.7 tonnes of white cocoa beans a year to make its white chocolate
fake.tell: White chocolate is cocoa butter with milk and sugar; there are no white cocoa beans that make it.

fake.h: Retired farmer, 61, drives a ride-on mower 480 km across {} in 9 hours at 30 km/h on average
fake.tell: Nine hours at 30 km/h covers only 270 km, not 480.

fake.h: Burglar in {} livestreams his break-in on a stolen 1995 iPhone, then falls asleep on the sofa
fake.tell: The iPhone launched in 2007, so no iPhone existed in 1995.

fake.h: After 38 years, a library in {} gets back an overdue book, a thriller published in 2009
fake.tell: A book borrowed 38 years ago cannot have been published in 2009.

fake.h: Metal detectorist in {} digs up a horned Viking helmet in a wheat field, and a museum buys it
fake.tell: Vikings did not wear horned helmets; that image is a 19th-century myth.

fake.h: Farmer in {} sells out of 304 bottles of premium bull milk at a weekend market
fake.tell: Bulls are male and do not produce milk.

fake.h: Amateur astronomer in {} sells 217 tickets to watch Halley's Comet from his garden in 2031
fake.tell: Halley's Comet next returns in 2061, not 2031.

fake.h: Cheesemaker in {} drills the holes in every wheel of his Emmental by hand, two hours per wheel
fake.tell: Emmental's holes are formed by gas from bacteria, not drilled.

fake.h: Parade in {} marks a man's sixth leap-day birthday; he says he was born on 29 February 2001
fake.tell: 2001 was not a leap year, so 29 February 2001 never existed.

fake.h: Time capsule from 1974 opens in {} to reveal a USB stick, a bowling ball and a ham roll
fake.tell: USB sticks did not exist until about 2000, so one cannot be in a 1974 capsule.

fake.h: Bakery in {} bakes 9,412 fortune cookies from a 640-year-old Beijing recipe for a fair
fake.tell: Fortune cookies are a 20th-century Californian/Japanese-American invention, not a Chinese medieval recipe.

fake.h: Farmer ploughing a field in {} turns up a 1,130-year-old Viking helmet with two curved horns
fake.tell: Vikings did not wear horned helmets; that image is a 19th-century stage invention.

fake.h: Museum in {} puts the guillotine that beheaded Anne Boleyn in 1536 on show for the first time
fake.tell: Anne Boleyn was beheaded with a sword, and the guillotine was not used until the 1790s.

fake.h: Choir in {} sings Handel's 2½-hour Messiah nine times back to back and finishes in 17 hours
fake.tell: Nine performances of 2.5 hours take 22.5 hours, not 17.

fake.h: Surgeons in {} remove a wad of chewing gum that a girl, 5, swallowed seven years ago
fake.tell: A 5-year-old girl was not yet born seven years ago.

fake.h: Cathedral in {} fits panes thicker at the bottom to mimic 680 years of glass slowly flowing
fake.tell: Glass does not flow at room temperature; old panes are uneven from how they were made.

fake.h: Café straddling the equator in {} charges tourists to watch sinks drain in opposite directions
fake.tell: The Coriolis effect is far too weak to steer water in a sink, so the direction is not set by hemisphere.

fake.h: Exhumed after three years, a farmer in {} had a beard 23 cm longer, the gravedigger says
fake.tell: Hair and nails do not keep growing after death; skin shrinks and only makes them look longer.
